### App configuration

The dist mount is served with fasthtml’s `StaticImmutable`. Vite’s
output uses content-hashed filenames, so a changed file always gets a
new URL, browsers can safely cache forever, and revalidating would be
pure waste. (`.vite/manifest.json` is served under the same mount
without a hashed name, but it’s only read from disk by
[`_mk_scripts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fhvite/core.html#_mk_scripts),
never fetched by browsers.)

With `run_build=True`, startup creates missing setup files, installs
dependencies with `pybun install` and runs `pybun run build`.
Installation follows the project’s lockfile. `directory` names the
project root; setup, builds and manifest reads use its `dirname`
subdirectory regardless of the process working directory.

With `run_build=False`, startup reads the existing manifest without
creating files, installing dependencies or building. Use this mode when
deployment has already built the assets.

With `dev=True`, startup installs dependencies and runs Vite on
localhost with hot module replacement. `port` defaults to 5173. An
occupied port fails startup rather than selecting another port. The app
header loads Vite’s client and the source entry point instead of a build
manifest. Shutdown stops Vite and its children, including when the app’s
own startup fails. `run_build` applies only when `dev=False`.

## Testing in a running app

``` python
server = JupyUviAsync(app)
await server.start()
with urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:5173/vite/@vite/client') as response: test_eq(response.status, 200)
Show = partial(HTMX, app=app)
```

A second app using the same Vite port fails startup. It does not attach
to the running Vite server.

``` python
other = FastHTML()
add_vite(other, dirname='vite', dev=True)
with expect_fail(RuntimeError, contains='Vite exited with status'):
    async with other.router.lifespan_context(other): pass
with urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:5173/vite/@vite/client') as response: test_eq(response.status, 200)
```
